This page is the entry to Phase 11. You have built your cohort in [Phase
10](build-study-population.qmd): a table with `pnr` and `index_date` per
person. Here you extract the outcomes and covariates for those people, one
register at a time, and save each extraction as its own `.rds` file. The table
below sends you to the page for each type of variable. In [Phase 12 - Assemble
and prepare the dataset](data-manipulation.qmd) you link the files into one
analysis dataset.

Gather everything you need from one register in one extraction: all the BEF
columns in one, all the LPR diagnoses in one, and so on.

## Filter to your cohort before `collect()` {#filter-before-collect}

You only need data on the people in your cohort. Filter each extraction to the
cohort while it is still lazy (in Arrow or DuckDB), so the whole population is
never pulled into R. Why this matters for speed and memory is explained in
[Phase 5](extraction-step-by-step.qmd).

```r
library(arrow) # open_dataset()
library(dplyr) # %>%, rename_with(), semi_join(), select(), collect()

cohort <- readRDS("path/to/full_cohort.rds")
cohort_pnrs <- unique(cohort$pnr) # vector with ALL pnr (exposed + comparator cohort)

register <- open_dataset("path/to/register/") %>%
  rename_with(tolower) %>%
  semi_join(tibble(pnr = cohort_pnrs), by = "pnr", copy = TRUE) %>% # keep only the cohort's rows - pushed down into Arrow (the lazy dataset), see Phase 5
  select(pnr, ...) %>% # select only the columns you need
  collect() # ONLY now is data pulled into R
```

## Which page for which variable? {#which-variables}

  | Type                                               | Page                                                       | Source                                               |
  | -------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
  | **Outcomes** (event date, censoring)               | [Outcomes](outcomes.qmd)                               | LPR (hospital diagnoses), DOD (deaths), VNDS (migrations) |
  | **Socioeconomics** (education, income, employment) | [Socioeconomic variables](socioeconomic-variables.qmd) | UDDA (education), FAIK (family income), AKM (labour market) |
  | **Immigrant status and country of origin**         | [Immigrants and descendants](immigrants-and-descendants.qmd) | BEF (`ie_type`, `opr_land`), VNDS (migrations)  |
  | **Parents' characteristics** (education, income at the child's birth) | [Family links](family-links.qmd#parent-characteristics) | BEF (`mor_id`, `far_id`), then the parent's own registers |
  | **Comorbidity** (conditions at baseline, Charlson) | [Comorbidity](comorbidity.qmd)                         | LPR diagnoses, LMDB prescriptions, or both           |
  | **Medication** (ATC exposure)                      | [Medication (ATC)](medication.qmd)                     | LMDB (prescriptions)                                 |
  | **Medication given in hospital**                   | [Hospital medication (SMR)](hospital-medication.qmd)   | SMR, held by the Danish Health Data Authority, not DST |
  | **Healthcare costs**                               | [Healthcare costs](healthcare-costs.qmd)               | DRG_KONTAKTER and DRG_SGHFORLOB (DRG-priced hospital contacts), sysi/sssy (primary sector fees), LMDB |
  | **Laboratory results** (one row per result)        | [Laboratory results](laboratory-results.qmd)           | LAB_F, the research table of the national laboratory database (Laboratoriedatabasens Forskertabel) |
  | **Demographics** (age, sex)                        | covered in [Phase 6](first-extraction.qmd)              | BEF (population)                                     |

Most pages follow the same pattern: open the register, filter to the cohort,
select or derive the variable, `collect()`, save as `.rds`. Start with
[Outcomes](outcomes.qmd) if you are working through the phase in order.
